subject: Goodness of fit for N-mixture model

messages.author: f7a50b8ee00ad283
messages.subject: Goodness of fit for N-mixture model
parts:
Dear all,
For N-mixture models fit via unmarked::pcount, the function AICcmodavg::Nmix.gof.test provides a goodness-of-fit test  based on a Pearson chi-squared statistic, compared to a bootstrapped reference distribution.  In these respects, it is similar to AICcmodavg:mb.gof.test for occupancy models.

The Mackenzie-Bailey test for occupancy models is based on the observed and expected frequencies of entire detection histories.  This test was well studied in Mackenzie and Bailey's original paper, and I believe it was shown to have good power to detect misspecification of the detection portion of the model, and less power to detect misspecification of the occupancy portion of the model.

A glance at the source code for Nmix.gof.test suggests that it is based on the sum of the squared residuals, where each residual is the difference between observed and expected counts at each site-visit.  I have two questions:
1) Has anybody studied the behavior of this test in any detail, similar to the simulation studies of Mackenzie and Bailey?
2) It seems to me that Nmix.gof.test, based on the sum of the squared residuals for each individual site-visit, might have somewhat less power to detect misspecifications of the detection probability than does the Mackenzie-Bailey statistic for occupancy models.  Is this accurate, way off base, or unknown?  
3) Does anybody have suggestions of particular discrepancy functions to use in posterior predictive checks of the goodness of fit of the N-mixture model?  Are any of these described or recommended in published literature?

An example that motivates my intuition in question 2:
Imagine that detectability was consistently lower on the first visit to each site, due to unmodeled heterogeneity in p or non-independence of visits.  Then the Mackenzie-Bailey statistic would respond strongly to the excess of detection histories beginning with zero.  But it seems to me that the Nmix.gof.test statistic would attribute this to usual sampling variance, without "noticing" that the variance is highly nonrandom with respect to the visit order.

Thanks in advance for your help, and of course thanks to the developers of unmarked and AICcmodavg!
Jacob Socolar

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: [unmarked] Goodness of fit for N-mixture model
parts:
Dear Jacob,

 

We have a little on this in section 6.8 of our recent AHM book, where in an admittedly little simulation we seemed to get some power of the Nmix GOF test to detect assumption violations. But in general, the topic of GOF assessment is way understudied for such hierarchical models in general. Lot remains to be done and learned.

 

Best regards  --- Marc

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: RE:[unmarked] Goodness of fit for N-mixture model
parts:
Dear Jacob,

For point 2, just to be clear, the test statistic for Nmix.gof.test( ) is based on the chi-square computed from the residuals as:

sum((obs - fits)^2/fits, na.rm = TRUE)

and not the sum of squared residuals per se.

Best,

Marc
